about: Free, open-source creative studios people use beside TribeCode. Linked, never bundled or downloaded by TribeCode: every url is the tool's own official site or download page (checked 2026-11-10). Licenses read from each project's LICENSE/COPYING file on 2026-11-10. Thumbnails are TribeCode-drawn tiles, not the projects' logos. 'for' uses server/sense.js kinds plus 'video' and 'any'.

studios.role: concept art, backgrounds and short clips
studios.title: ArtCraft
studios.what: AI images and video, plus native apps for editing and design.
studios.good: Concept art, backgrounds, characters, product shots, social posts and short trailers, with the image and video models you choose.
studios.back: Export PNG or WebP images and MP4 clips, then drop them into Files › Assets.

studios.title: Blender
studios.good: Characters, props and whole scenes for 3D games and websites; renders and turntables for trailers.
studios.back: Export glTF (.glb) for three.js or Godot, or render PNG/MP4. glTF files open in TribeCode's 3D viewer.

studios.role: painted art, splash screens and illustrations
studios.title: Krita
studios.good: Hand-painted art, textures, splash screens, comics and illustrations for sites and games.
studios.back: Export PNG (with transparency) or WebP into assets/images.

studios.title: Pixelorama
studios.what: Pixel art editor for sprites, tiles and animations.
studios.good: Characters, enemies, tilesets and animated sprite sheets for 2D games.
studios.back: Export a PNG sprite sheet (and its frame size) into assets/sprites; the game can use it directly.

studios.role: the levels and the playable game
studios.title: Godot
studios.good: Building levels and whole games with a visual editor, physics and animation.
studios.back: Export to Web (HTML5) into the code repository and it runs in TribeCode's preview.

studios.title: LMMS
studios.what: Music production with beats, synths and samples.
studios.good: Soundtracks, loops and jingles for games, videos and ads.
studios.back: Export OGG or WAV into assets/audio and credit yourself in assets/CREDITS.md.

studios.title: Audacity
studios.good: Voice-overs, podcasts, cleaning up sound effects and trimming music.
studios.back: Export OGG or WAV into assets/audio.

studios.title: Kdenlive
studios.what: Video editing with a full timeline.
studios.good: Trailers, launch videos, tutorials and devlogs.
studios.back: Export MP4 (H.264) and put it on the project's website or in Files.

studios.title: Penpot
studios.what: Design and prototyping in the browser.
studios.good: Screens, layouts, icons and clickable prototypes for apps and websites, together with the team.
studios.back: Export SVG or PNG into assets/, or hand the CSS and measurements to your AI helper.

studios.title: Material Maker
studios.good: Seamless textures (wood, stone, metal) for 3D scenes in three.js or Godot.
studios.back: Export PNG texture maps into assets/textures.

studios.title: BeepBox
studios.good: Quick retro tunes for pixel games, no install.
studios.back: Export WAV or MP3 into assets/audio.

studios.title: OBS Studio
studios.good: Recording gameplay and demos, streaming build nights, capturing footage for trailers.
studios.back: Record MP4, then cut it in Kdenlive or Shotcut.

studios.title: Shotcut
studios.good: Fast cuts for short clips, social videos and demos.
studios.back: Export MP4 for the website or social posts.

studios.role: a no-code version or prototype of the game
studios.title: GDevelop
studios.good: Making a game with events instead of code, great for beginners in the tribe.
studios.back: Export to HTML5 into the code repository so it runs in the preview.

studios.role: a Lua version of the game
studios.title: LÖVE
studios.good: Small, fast 2D games written in Lua.
studios.back: Keep the Lua code in the repository; your AI helpers can work on it there.

studios.role: a lightweight version of the game
studios.title: raylib
studios.what: Simple library for programming games in C and many other languages.
studios.good: Learning game programming and making lightweight games.
studios.back: Build for the web (WebAssembly) to run it in the preview.

studios.role: a Rust version of the game
studios.title: Bevy
studios.good: Ambitious 2D and 3D games for teams who like Rust.
studios.back: Build for the web (WebAssembly) to run it in the preview.

studios.role: a Rust version with a full editor
studios.title: Fyrox
studios.what: Game engine with a scene editor, in Rust.
studios.good: 3D and 2D games with a full editor, for Rust teams.
studios.back: Keep the project in the code repository; export builds from the editor.

studios.title: Stride
studios.good: High-end 3D and VR projects in C#.
studios.back: Keep the project in the code repository; share builds as downloads.

studios.role: a tiny retro version in Python
studios.title: Pyxel
studios.good: Tiny retro games in Python, with a built-in sprite and sound editor.
studios.back: Export to HTML so it runs in TribeCode's preview.

studios.title: TIC-80
studios.what: Fantasy computer for tiny retro games.
studios.good: Game-jam sized games with built-in code, sprite, map and music editors.
studios.back: Export to HTML so it runs in TribeCode's preview.

studios.title: Twine
studios.good: Story games, choose-your-path tutorials and narrative prototypes.
studios.back: Publish to a single HTML file in the repository; it runs in the preview.

helps.game: For a game: sprites and tiles in Pixelorama, levels in Godot, music in LMMS or BeepBox, and a trailer from Kdenlive when you launch.
helps.3d: For a 3D project: models in Blender, textures in Material Maker, and Godot or three.js to show them.
helps.site: For a website: layouts and icons in Penpot, images in Krita or ArtCraft, and a short video for the front page.
helps.app: For an app: screens and prototypes in Penpot, icons and images in Krita or ArtCraft, and a demo video.
helps.bot: For a bot: an avatar and banner from ArtCraft or Krita, and a short demo clip.
helps.tool: For a tool: an icon and screenshots, and a short screen recording in OBS.
helps.api: For an API: a logo and diagrams, and a screen recording of it in use.
helps.notes: For notes and docs: illustrations from Krita or ArtCraft, and voice notes cleaned up in Audacity.
helps.video: For videos and marketing: record in OBS, cut in Kdenlive or Shotcut, add music from LMMS.
helps.other: Make the pictures, sound and video your project needs, then bring the files back into Files › Assets.
